title: refactor(cli): decouple useGeminiStream from lookahead logic for parallel agents

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue clearly describes an architectural problem in useGeminiStream.ts where UI lookahead logic is used to stitch together parallel agent executions. It identifies the target files and explains how packages/core should be refactored to emit structured ToolBatch/Turn objects instead.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: Decoupling useGeminiStream from tactical lookahead logic requires refactoring event/batch representations in packages/core and updating the UI streaming hooks in packages/cli to process structured batch events, making it a cross-package refactor.

summary.problem: useGeminiStream in packages/cli currently uses tactical lookahead logic and refs to stitch together contiguous parallel agent tool calls to prevent UI tearing when agents finish out of sync.
summary.root_cause: packages/core does not emit structured ToolBatch or Turn semantic boundaries for parallel agent executions, forcing the UI layer to handle batch completion timing manually.
summary.context: Moving batch boundary responsibility from the UI layer (useGeminiStream) to packages/core simplifies UI state management and ensures robust rendering of parallel agent executions.

steps: Define structured ToolBatch or Turn abstractions in packages/core to encapsulate execution boundaries for tool and agent calls.
Update scheduler and turn handling in packages/core to emit ToolBatch objects when parallel executions complete.
Refactor useGeminiStream in packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.ts to consume core-emitted batch objects directly.
Remove lookahead logic and contiguous agent timing refs from useGeminiStream.ts.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: useGeminiStream renders parallel agent execution results based on semantic batch boundaries emitted from core without implementing UI-side lookahead logic.
verification_steps: Run unit tests for useGeminiStream in packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx using Vitest.
Verify tool execution batch rendering when handling parallel agent tools.
Ensure no regressions in stream output ordering or tool completion handling.
